questions.stem: Why is the left ventricular myocardium thicker than the right ventricular myocardium?
options: It pumps against greater systemic resistance
It receives blood from the pulmonary artery
It opens the tricuspid valve
It fills from the venae cavae
questions.explanation: The systemic circuit presents greater resistance and requires higher pressure than the short pulmonary circuit.

questions.stem: At which pressure relationship should an atrioventricular valve open?

questions.explanation: AV valves open when atrial pressure becomes greater than ventricular pressure, allowing ventricular filling.

questions.stem: Damage to the sinoatrial node most directly disrupts:

questions.explanation: The sinoatrial node normally acts as the heart's pacemaker and initiates each wave of cardiac excitation.

questions.stem: The one-cell-thick capillary wall mainly improves exchange by:
